body:
This is an intentional API decision that lets you use [multiple components as named children](https://github.com/rackt/react-router/blob/master/docs/api/Route.md#components) in a single route component.

`this.props.children` is an opaque type that is being used by many different React libraries to mean something other than just node, array, or `null`. In [react-motion](https://github.com/chenglou/react-motion)'s `<Spring>` component, for example, `this.props.children` is a function.

issue.title: resolveStyles breaks this.props.children if children is an object, not an array

repository.name: radium
repository.description: A toolchain for React component styling.

issue.body:
This issue is related to #317, but is different enough that I thought I'd post a new issue instead of commenting there.

react-router sets `this.props.children` to be a [keyed object](https://github.com/rackt/react-router/blob/master/docs/api/Route.md#components). `_resolveChildren` uses `React.Children.map` to iterate over that object, and the result of calling that map function is a broken object that can't be used anywhere.

My gut tells me this is an issue with react-router, but an issue posted there was [closed with the explanation](https://github.com/rackt/react-router/issues/1968) that: "`this.props.children` is an opaque type that is being used by many different React libraries to mean something other than just node, array, or `null`. In react-motion's <Spring> component, for example, this.props.children is a function."

In any case, the interaction between these two libraries is causing issues. Can we fix this on the radium side (e.g. check [`childrenType`](https://github.com/FormidableLabs/radium/blob/master/modules/resolve-styles.js#L45) before calling `React.Children.map`)?

body:
From the React v0.14 Release Candidate breaking changes notes :

> Plain objects are no longer supported as React children; arrays should be used instead. You can use the createFragment helper to migrate, which now returns an array.

Isn't this going to cause problems ?
So maybe rename it to `routeComponents` or something?

Why was the decision made to keep this in `children`, and not pass them as props instead?

As I mentioned in https://github.com/FormidableLabs/radium/issues/358#issuecomment-140833140:

> This is not the same as `react-motion`, where they've created a component that _accepts_ a different type for `children`. `react-router` is _passing_ a different type for `children` to normal components, one that is not inline with the rest of React.

I think @ianobermiller is right in this case. We should probably give people a `children` object that looks like other `children` objects. Accepting a different kind of `children` as a prop is a different discussion.
@mjackson thanks for following up. Will you go with children as props instead?
@ianobermiller Ya, that's probably what we'll do. Not 100% sure yet.
Another option might be not to use children at all, and just use props with the specified names, e.g. `this.props.sidebar` and `this.props.content`.

issue.title: Accomodate multiple components in a route?

repository.name: react-router-relay
repository.description: [Deprecated] Relay Classic integration for React Router

issue.body:
In the sidebar example, multiple components are specified for a route.
https://github.com/rackt/react-router/blob/master/examples/sidebar/app.js#L102

Should this be possible with relay? Would the `queries` parameter need to accept an object mapping queries to the multiple components? Like:

``` jsx
<Route components={{sidebar: Sidebar, content: Content}}
       queries={{sidebar: sidebarQueries, content: contentQueries}}>...</Route>
```

 Or, perhaps the queries could be available for all the (relay) components.

``` jsx
<Route components={{sidebar: Sidebar, content: Content}}
       queries={routeQueries}>...</Route>
```

body: @taion that is exactly what I meant by "children as props" :)

+1

``` jsx
<Route component={Page}>
```

would just be a shortcut for:

``` jsx
<Route components={{ main: Page }}>
```

and the component is available in `this.props.main`. Although IMO it shouldn't be at the root: 

``` es6
const { main, someOtherPartial } = this.props.outlets
```
